Battling the Beast: A Guide to Taming Dallisgrass in Louisiana’s Warm-Season Grasses

Learn how to identify, control, and prevent Dallisgrass in centipede, Bermuda, St. Augustine, and Zoysia lawns across South Louisiana.

By Grow Green Weed Control • Updated May 2024 • 4–5 min read

Hey there, fellow lawn warriors! If you’ve ever found yourself in a heated battle with an unruly invader known as Dallisgrass in your lush Louisiana lawn—fear not! You’re not alone in this green warfare. Today, we’re diving deep into the trenches to explore the ins and outs of this pesky plant, its challenges, and the best strategies to reclaim your turf supremacy across the land of centipede, Bermuda, St. Augustine, and Zoysia.

🌾 Meet the Foe: Dallisgrass

Picture this: you step out into your yard, basking in the warm Louisiana sunshine, only to be greeted by tall, clumpy grasses that seem to mock your efforts at a pristine lawn. Enter Dallisgrass — the arch-nemesis of lawn aficionados across the South. With its coarse texture and prolific seed production, Dallisgrass spreads like wildfire, choking out your beloved turf faster than you can say “weed killer.”

Pro Tip: Dallisgrass thrives in thin, compacted turf. Regular aeration and dense turf coverage are your first defense.

⚔️ The Battle Plan: How to Kill Dallisgrass

Now that you’ve identified the enemy, it’s time to formulate your battle plan. But beware — Dallisgrass is a formidable foe, known for its resilience and stubborn nature. Here are some tried-and-tested tactics to send it packing:

  • Manual Removal: Roll up your sleeves and get ready to pull some weeds! Effective for small infestations, especially after rain when soil is soft.
  • Chemical Warfare: When manual labor won’t cut it, use selective herbicides with active ingredients like quinclorac or fluazifop-p-butyl that target Dallisgrass without harming your desired turf.
  • Cultural Practices: Maintain proper mowing height and watering practices to promote healthy turf and discourage Dallisgrass growth. Aerate regularly to improve drainage and reduce compaction.
  • Prevention is Key: Apply a pre-emergent herbicide each spring to prevent new Dallisgrass seed germination before it starts.
Important: Dallisgrass is a perennial weed. Post-emergent treatments may require multiple applications over time for complete control.

🌤️ Navigating the Terrain: Challenges & Best Practices for Louisiana Lawns

Louisiana’s humid subtropical climate adds unique challenges to lawn care. Each warm-season grass has different needs. Here’s how they stack up:

Grass TypeStrengthsWatch For
CentipedeLow maintenance, loves acidic soils and humidity.Over-fertilizing and cold damage.
BermudaFast growth and heat tolerant.Thatch buildup — dethatch yearly to stay healthy.
St. AugustineThick carpet look, good shade tolerance.Susceptible to fungus if overwatered.
ZoysiaFine texture and drought resistant.Slow to establish — be patient with new lawns.

🏁 Victory in Sight: Key Takeaways

  • Identify and treat Dallisgrass early before seed heads form.
  • Maintain a dense, healthy turf to crowd out invaders.
  • Use pre-emergent in spring and spot-treat with selective post-emergent herbicides.
  • Be consistent — one season of vigilance beats years of infestation.
